$comment: Declares which "deprecated" docs/contracts/package-lifecycle.json packages are DELIBERATELY still live on the registry, and why. A deprecated package remaining installable is not automatically wrong -- that is the entire point of deprecation: existing consumers keep resolving it while new adoption is steered at the replacement -- but it must be a declared decision, not silent drift indistinguishable from a package nobody remembered to unpublish. See scripts/check-package-visibility.mjs, which joins this file against the registry's own package list. A "deprecated" package live on the registry with no entry here, or with an entry whose reviewBy date has passed, is a gate finding: either declare (or renew) the retention, or remove the package from the registry. Same reason+reviewBy shape as packages/controller's dependency-scope allowlist (see its own doc comment) -- a standing exemption with no expiry is the same failure as an absence with no declared reason, just wearing the other sign.

packages.name: @vespeneventures/auth
packages.reason: Deprecated into @vespeneventures/bouncer per issue #458. Kept live so a consumer already pinned to a published auth version keeps resolving it while migrating. No forwarding stub ships, deliberately: a stub would keep the old name importable and a supersession check could then never reach zero.
